recommendations.action: Split the 90-minute biology lecture with a 15-minute screen-free break
recommendations.rationale: Unbroken cognitive and screen demand can intensify fogginess and headache. Adding structured pauses maintains task tolerance.
recommendations.whatWeInferred: Extended continuous screen exposure without pauses compounds sensory fatigue.
recommendations.whatWeDoNotKnow: Whether institutional assignment deadlines permit flexible interval completion.

recommendations.action: Relocate lunch in busy campus cafeteria to a calmer, quieter setting or step out for quiet breaks
recommendations.rationale: Loud, visually intense, or crowded spaces quickly deplete sensory tolerance when recovering from concussion.
recommendations.whatWeInferred: Concurrent auditory and visual stimuli aggravate light and noise sensitivity.
recommendations.whatWeDoNotKnow: Whether a private or quiet alternative space is readily accessible on-site.

recommendations.action: Insert a 20-minute quiet decompression window before the afternoon demand stack
recommendations.rationale: Today's capacity baseline is reduced due to sleep and mood symptoms. Proactive pacing prevents late-day symptom flare-ups.
recommendations.whatWeInferred: Multiple consecutive commitments without recovery buffers lead to demand outpacing baseline capacity.
recommendations.whatWeDoNotKnow: Exact personal fatigue thresholds across different study tasks.

recommendations.action: Maintain low-stress social check-ins with friends or trusted colleagues
recommendations.rationale: Concussion recovery is emotionally taxing. Staying connected in low-demand ways helps reduce anxiety and mood strain.
recommendations.whatWeInferred: Concussion symptoms often include irritability and nervousness that benefit from supportive social pacing.
recommendations.whatWeDoNotKnow: Personal comfort level discussing recovery needs with peers.

evidence.title: Sleep hygiene: limit screens and loud sound before bed
evidence.claim: The CDC suggests limiting screen time and loud music before bed, sleeping in a dark room, and keeping a fixed bedtime and wake-up schedule while recovering.

evidence.title: Do not cocoon in a dark room; relative rest instead
evidence.claim: Concussion Alliance advises against lying in a darkened room resting for extended periods during the day, even in the first 24 to 48 hours, recommending relative rest that includes activities of daily living.

evidence.title: Early return to school can shorten recovery and reduce mental health symptoms
evidence.claim: The CDC states that most children can return to school within one to two days of a concussion even while experiencing symptoms, and that early return can shorten recovery and reduce the likelihood of mental health symptoms.

evidence.title: Limiting screen time in the first two days is associated with faster recovery
evidence.claim: Concussion Alliance reports research in which limiting screen use to roughly 65 minutes per day for the first two days was associated with substantially faster recovery, with gradual symptom-tolerant resumption after 48 hours.

evidence.title: Physical and sensory accommodations: rest breaks and transition time
evidence.claim: For physical and sensory symptoms the CDC suggests providing rest breaks, allowing extra time to move between classes, and allowing time to visit the school nurse.

evidence.title: Emotional support: someone to talk to, and staying connected
evidence.claim: The CDC suggests developing a plan for who a student can talk to if they feel overwhelmed, and encouraging them to stay connected to friends during recovery.

evidence.title: Fatigue and low energy are recognised concussion symptoms
evidence.claim: The CDC lists feeling tired and having no energy as physical symptoms of mild TBI and concussion.

evidence.title: Return to learn precedes return to sport, under clinician oversight
evidence.claim: The 6th International Consensus Statement on Concussion in Sport describes return to learn as preceding full return to sport, with clinician oversight of progression.
